limits: This verdict reviews retained receipts and source sections; no provider acquisition, calendar execution or comparison was rerun.
GitHub blob retrieval failed for ten adopted candidates; all eleven pinned README files were subsequently read successfully through their raw.githubusercontent.com equivalents.
Private acquisition payloads and runtime artifacts were not opened or independently rehashed. Their verification is reported by the retained receipts.
Upstream README examples establish source-review evidence only. Release metadata and broader product claims were not independently validated.
Non-adopted candidates have no retained evidence references in the packet; none is established as a superior challenger.
open_gaps: The selected set provides bounded acquisition and reference capabilities; it does not fully satisfy licensed, historically eligible, reproducible all-equities research.
Authenticated access does not establish all storage, redistribution, derived-data or real-time entitlements.
Alpaca acceptance covers one retrospective AAPL sample. Delistings, ticker reuse, permanent security identity, complete corporate actions and an as-known historical universe remain unestablished.
The dividend's missing currency prevents complete cash-unit reconciliation despite matching numeric values.
SEC acceptance times and newly observed source bytes do not establish original historical dissemination or observation. The five sampled headers remain ineligible at the historical cutoff.
Calendar execution establishes one XNYS session, not comprehensive holidays, emergency closures, extended hours or security-specific halts.
Immutable capture and cutoff rejection depend on project-local adapters. Native SDKs alone do not establish those guarantees, and the Alpaca adapter uses pinned private transport seams.
No executed provider comparison establishes superiority on representative universe coverage, correction semantics, cost, latency and historical availability.

arms: Baseline: retained Alpaca acquisition and frozen LEAN reconciliation, EdgarTools SEC acquisition with the local provenance gate, and the recorded XNYS calendar result.
Challenger: Massive or Databento observations for the same frozen securities and dates, normalized to the existing comparison contract with retained source bytes, rights and availability evidence.
Negative controls: corrupted source bytes, late observations, ambiguous timestamps and missing acceptance metadata exercised through the existing provenance tests.
overturn_protocol.metric: Compare exact raw-close agreement, missing or extra sessions, action-value and currency reconciliation, source-hash reproducibility, and rejection before demonstrated availability. Require documented permitted use and historical identity coverage; measure acquisition cost and latency on identical scope. A replacement must close a demonstrated gap without weakening existing checks.

overturn_when: Change the verdict after an executed comparison using blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/compare.py shows a candidate improves the retained acquisition or corporate-action reconciliation, with independently supported rights, identity and historical availability; preserve the rejection behavior checked by python3 -m unittest tests.test_catalyst_provenance. Calendar replacement additionally requires an executed comparison against blueprints/us-equities/data/summarize_backtest.py and evidence covering the newly required sessions. Passing synthetic gate tests alone cannot promote a provider.
why_selected: Select alpaca-py for bounded market observations, EdgarTools for SEC reference data, and exchange_calendars for session boundaries. Retained native execution in blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/native-receipt.json records Alpaca-py GET transport acquiring 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars and two corporate actions across five HTTP 200 pages; its measured comparison matched all 25 closes and both numeric action values, while dividend currency remained unknown. blueprints/us-equities/catalyst-provenance/access-resolution.json records native EdgarTools acquisition of 371 CIK/accession entries representing 360 unique accessions. Separately identified local integration acquired five headers and rejected all five at the historical cutoff, qualifying them only after current observation. blueprints/us-equities/data/receipt.json records native XNYS boundaries for 2013-10-07, corroborated by the calendar calls in summarize_backtest.py. These complementary bounded results provide stronger task evidence than README-only alternatives; they do not establish complete historical eligibility or data rights.
